incidents.victim: US federal agencies (Federal Reserve, DOE, DOJ, Senate, NASA, HHS/NIH)
incidents.attacker: China — Ministry of State Security and PLA military intelligence
incidents.vector: Contractor Nanjing Xinjiuwei ran the 'QScan' scanner and 'QTRouter' obfuscation network to infect IoT devices and route intrusions, hiding the true origin of attacks dating to 2018.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized the platforms, rendering both tools inoperable; the affidavit ties the operation to breaches of numerous federal agencies, hospitals, telecoms, power companies and defense contractors, including a 2026 intrusion at the US Senate.

incidents.victim: Organizations running exposed AI infrastructure (LiteLLM, RAGFlow, Kestra)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited exposed AI gateways and orchestration surfaces (chaining flaws such as CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710 in LiteLLM) to gain code execution, harvest credentials from process environments, and access backend databases.
incidents.impact: Microsoft observed credential and API-key theft, PostgreSQL data collection, XMRig cryptominer deployment and SSH-key persistence across compromised AI workloads, treating these control points as high-value targets.

incidents.vector: An actor using the persona 'CyberLeek' obtained pre-release Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay footage, likely via an insider with access to a game build, and published it publicly with crypto-wallet watermarks.
incidents.impact: One of the year's highest-profile data-extortion cases; daily leaks continued for over a week while Take-Two pursued DMCA subpoenas against Discord, Microsoft, X and Google to unmask those responsible.

incidents.vector: The Akira ransomware gang breached the benefits-administration platform's network in November 2025 and exfiltrated files before disrupting systems.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole Social Security numbers, financial account data, health insurance and medical information, passport numbers and taxpayer IDs on tens of thousands of people; class-action lawsuits are being organized.

incidents.vector: A large distributed denial-of-service attack flooded the infrastructure of Digdir's IT partner Vivicta, two to three times larger than prior incidents.
incidents.impact: Ten digital services were disrupted for roughly 30 hours, including the ID-porten identity gateway used by 4.5 million people, affecting logins to public services and parts of Norway's health and e-prescription systems; no data was accessed.

incidents.vector: A North Korean espionage group breached the Presidential Office in February 2026 as part of a broader campaign; the initial access method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The campaign racked up more than 100 victims by April, including universities, police departments, news agencies and hospitals; South Korean authorities are still investigating.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the healthcare provider's internal network and stole confidential and sensitive data; the intrusion method was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Nutex, which operates 27 medical facilities across 12 US states, disclosed the breach to the SEC but provided no further detail on scope or affected individuals.

incidents.vector: The pro-Kremlin group NoName057 compiled and leaked personal data on Telegram, citing Spain's support for Ukraine.
incidents.impact: Names of nearly 1,000 members of the Spanish military and police forces were exposed; authorities linked the release to a former professor who fled to Russia.

incidents.victim: Victims of West African fraud networks (Black Axe)
incidents.vector: Interpol's Operation Jackal IV targeted organized fraud networks running business email compromise, romance and investment scams, money laundering and sextortion across 22 countries.
incidents.impact: 58 arrests and 263 identified suspects; seizures included millions in cash and crypto and hundreds of blocked bank accounts tied to schemes such as a 143 million-euro investment scam.

incidents.vector: State-sponsored actors attempted to compromise the messaging accounts of high-ranking EU officials, apparently linked to earlier Signal and WhatsApp phishing operations.
incidents.impact: Disclosed in a closed CERT-EU presentation; details remain limited but the activity targets senior officials' encrypted communications.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure, universities and government agencies
incidents.attacker: Iran — Ministry of Intelligence (MOIS) and IRGC, via the Mabna Institute
incidents.vector: The Tehran-based Mabna Institute conducted spearphishing and credential theft against university faculty accounts and, since 2023, breached energy, defense, healthcare, IT and financial-sector targets on behalf of Iranian intelligence.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed a superseding indictment charging 17 individuals over the theft of 31.5 terabytes of academic data and IP, and Treasury sanctioned six MOIS-directed hackers; the group also targeted US Labor Department, FERC and UN email accounts.

incidents.vector: Iranian hackers — reportedly the same actors who breached US water utilities — compromised operational technology, with reports of an unsecured programmable logic controller (PLC).
incidents.impact: A small British power plant was forced offline for four days; no customers lost power and the wider grid was unaffected, but officials called it a major escalation from earlier water-utility targeting.

incidents.vector: Attackers used a social-engineering attack in early July to breach Apollo's cloud systems, part of a broader wave hitting US investment and Wall Street firms.
incidents.impact: Apollo confirmed a data breach in a notification to the California attorney general; the incident is tied to an ongoing campaign against the financial sector.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited CVE-2026-73570, an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Zimbra servers with SNMP notifications enabled (on by default in vulnerable versions), via crafted SMTP requests.
incidents.impact: CISA added the bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and set a three-day federal patch deadline after CERT Polska reported an active exploitation campaign; compromised servers expose email, calendars and contacts for follow-on attacks.

incidents.vector: The attacker allegedly abused the protocol's anti-theft defenses to trick the platform into unwanted loans, reportedly using an AI tool to chain exploits across six smaller unrelated bugs.
incidents.impact: Roughly $1.7 million in crypto-assets was stolen from the platform.

incidents.vector: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party software application to access the Toronto pediatric hospital's systems.
incidents.impact: Personal data of hospital employees was stolen; SickKids said no patient data was exposed and offered 24 months of credit monitoring to affected staff.

incidents.vector: The ShinyHunters group listed the security firm on its dark-web leak site; ReliaQuest says the actors phished one employee and reached an Okta backend in view-only mode.
incidents.impact: ReliaQuest denied a meaningful breach, stating repeated attempts to access backend apps were blocked; ShinyHunters has provided no proof of its claims.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the French telecom operator and exfiltrated customer records in an incident disclosed the following month.
incidents.impact: More than 2.1 million customers were affected; exposed data included names, postal addresses, phone numbers and contract details, with IP addresses and equipment details for some.

incidents.victim: Global technology, staffing, healthcare and fintech employers
incidents.vector: North Korean IT operators (tracked as PurpleDelta), likely based in China, used 22+ fabricated personas, AI-generated photos, custom ChatGPT assistants and real-time AI interview tools to secure remote technical jobs.
incidents.impact: Operators applied to over 1,100 companies and were likely actively employed at ten or more organizations, recording internal meetings and posing a material insider-threat and sanctions-evasion risk that funds the DPRK regime.
